papers_read.title_as_printed: Predicting Conversion from MCI to AD Combining Multi-Modality Data and Based on Molecular Subtype (Li et al., Brain Sci. 2021)
Early MCI-to-AD Conversion Prediction Using Future Value Forecasting of Multimodal Features (Minhas et al., Comput. Intell. Neurosci. 2021)

what_each_reports.P-179: MCI-CPS (subtype-specific VBpMKL) on baseline sMRI ROI volumes + blood SNP + blood mRNA; 3-year conversion; ADNI-1 MCI n=125, 5-fold CV AUC 0.8260; external ADNI-GO/2 AUC 0.7809.
what_each_reports.P-186: Linear SVM on longitudinal trajectories of neuropsychological measures + MRI morphometry, where two observed visits are extended by a forecast third value; MCIp = conversion before month 36, ADNI-1. 6-month-ahead AUC 91.2% (n=119, 19 markers); 1-year-ahead AUC 95.7% (n=85, 9 markers); 5-fold CV. MRI-only 1-year AUC 90.5%, 6-month 88%.

quantity_a: ROC-AUC for 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion from a single baseline visit; predictors = sMRI ROI volumes + blood genomics/transcriptomics; ADNI-1 MCI n=125; 5-fold CV.
quantity_b: ROC-AUC for conversion before month 36 using three-point trajectories (two observed visits 6 or 12 months apart + one forecast value) of neuropsychological and MRI markers; ADNI-1 MCI with complete consecutive visits (n=85 for the 0.957 figure); 5-fold CV.
incompatible_if_same: No. Neither paper evaluates the other's input, neither reports an interval excluding the other's value, and P-186's own authors attribute the 0.957 to including 'the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classification feature', a feature P-179 cannot have.

gates.task: match: both T2 with a roughly 3-year window, but P-186 requires two or three longitudinal visits and scores trajectories, not a baseline visit.
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI-1 MCI in both; participant overlap likely.
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal 5-fold CV for the cited figures.
gates.modality_family: mismatch, not waived: P-179 = sMRI + blood SNP/mRNA; P-186 = neuropsychological measures + sMRI morphometry. No PET in either.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (ROC-AUC) and similar outcome window, but a different input representation (single baseline visit vs forecast longitudinal trajectories), different predictor sets and a different eligible population (complete 6- or 12-monthly visit sequences).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.957 is below 0.97 and the pack marks both false. P-186's 'ground truth' benchmark reaches 98% but that is not the proposed method's figure; the internal-only, n=85 design is noted as a caution.
independence: Distinct author groups; both samples are drawn from ADNI-1 MCI, so shared participants are likely (non-independence noted, not disqualifying).
grounds: Different input representation: P-186 classifies longitudinal marker trajectories that include a forecast value at the time of conversion, while P-179 uses a single baseline visit.
Different predictor sets: neuropsychological tests + MRI (P-186) against sMRI + blood SNP/mRNA (P-179); the modality-family gate fails with no waiver on record.
Different eligible populations and sample sizes (n=85 with three annual readings vs n=125 ADNI-1 MCI at baseline).
No result would be incompatible even on a shared quantity: neither study claims an ordering the other refutes.

evidence_quotes.quote: The results show that the AUC of MCI-CPS (5-fold) was 0.8260 (81.82% sensitivity, 77.08% speciﬁcity, 80.00% accuracy).
a subtyping-based prediction strategy to predict the conversion from MCI to AD in three years according to MCI patient subtypes.
Te proposed technique resulted in a high classiﬁcation AUC of 91.2% and 95.7% for 6-month- and 1-year-ahead AD prediction, respectively, using multimodal markers.
for 1-year-ahead prediction, the dataset contains three consecutive annual readings, resulting in 35 MCIp and 50 MCIs subjects.

Te method proposed in this paper has recorded the highest classiﬁcation AUC of 95.7% predominantly because of involving the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classiﬁcation feature.

record_defects: claim_b gives P-186 'AUC 0.957' while the registry row gives 'AUC 0.912'; these are two different analyses (1-year-ahead, n=85 vs 6-month-ahead, n=119), and the record does not say which it means.
The registry labels both papers' Modality 'MRI/PET'; neither uses PET.
resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine' on a gap test while the resolution field says 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch'.
The bridging-evidence list is a generic dump of T2 ADNI papers with no stated separating condition.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Both studies scoring the same input representation (baseline-only or the same longitudinal design) with the same predictor families, with non-overlapping uncertainty.
